title: Compression stockings and socks | NHS inform
text:
Compression stockings and socks
Compression stockings or socks are used to help blood circulation or pain.
What are compression stockings and socks used for?
Compression stockings and socks are often used to help improve blood flow in your lower legs. The elastic in them puts pressure on your legs, ankles and feet. This helps prevent blood and fluid from building up in these areas.
Your GP or healthcare professional may prescribe compression stockings or socks for conditions that cause poor blood circulation. These include:
chronic venous insufficiency – a common condition that affects veins in the legs
varicose veins
– a condition where the veins are swollen and twisted in the legs
deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
– a blood clot that develops within the vein, usually in the leg
swelling of the feet, ankles or legs – where fluid becomes trapped in the muscle tissue
leg ulcer
– a long-lasting (chronic) sore that usually develops on the inside of the leg
How compression stockings and socks work
Compression stockings and socks put pressure on your lower legs. This helps to improve your blood flow and can also help with swelling and pain.
Wearing compression stockings and socks can also:
prevent new
varicose veins
control
high blood pressure (hypertension)
in your leg veins
prevent blood clots
help with muscle recovery
Types of compression stockings and socks
There are different types of compression stockings and socks. These are split into 3 different groups called classes. These are:
class 1 – stockings or socks that give light compression
class 2 – stockings or socks that give medium compression
class 3 – stockings or socks that give high compression
Your GP, healthcare professional or local pharmacist will discuss your symptoms and will be able to tell you which compression stockings or socks will work best for you.
They’ll also be able to tell you:
how to put on your compression stockings or socks
how long you should wear them
Non medical compression stockings and socks for sports and travel are also available to buy online and in shops. They are designed to:
improve circulation
reduce swelling
help muscle fatigue
Non medical compression stockings and socks can be worn during long periods of no movement or physical exercise.
How to get used to compression stockings or socks
Make sure you put on your stockings or socks as instructed by your healthcare professional.
There are some steps you can take to help you get used to wearing your compression stockings or socks.
Do
put on your compression stockings or socks as early as possible in the morning
make sure your skin is dry and any moisturisers or lotions have been absorbed completely before putting your stockings or socks on
Don’t
do not fold or wrinkle the material when wearing your compression stockings or socks
do not wear them to bed, unless you have been instructed by your healthcare professional
avoid sharp fingernails or jewellery that could damage the stockings or socks and your skin
You may use talcum powder if your skin is moist. This can make it easier to put on your compression stockings or socks.
Looking after your compression stockings or socks
You should be given two pairs of compression stockings or socks. You should wear one pair while the other is being washed and dried.
When washing your compression stockings or socks, you should:
wash them on their own the first time
wash them by hand or on the delicate cycle of your washing machine
let them dry naturally – do not squeeze the water out of your stockings or socks
dry them away from direct heat – do not dry them in a tumble dryer or on a radiator
wash the stockings every day if you use ointment on your legs
